transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. I came in today because... well, I just can't stop feeling like I'm a danger and a disappointment. I had a near-miss at work recently—I'm a nurse—and it just... it really feels like it proves I'm not meant to be doing this job. Honestly, I just keep thinking that everyone would be better off without me.
Are you thinking about killing yourself right now?

No, I'm not... I don't have a plan to kill myself or anything like that. But I do keep having these thoughts. Like... maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up tomorrow. Or if I could just disappear, you know? That way I wouldn't be able to mess anything else up.
Do these feelings seem mostly connected to the near-miss at work?

I'm not really sure. Um... I guess I haven't really thought about whether it's just connected to that. The near-miss is just what's on my mind the most right now, but I don't know if that's the only reason I've been feeling like this.
Aside from the near-miss at work, have you been feeling this down in other parts of your life too?

Yeah, I think I have. It's not just about what happened the other day. Most days, I just wake up with this really heavy, empty feeling in my chest. And... even when I'm at the clinic, you know, smiling at my patients in Spanish and just trying to act normal, I feel like I'm barely holding myself together. It just feels like it's always there in the background.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. I used to do a lot of things to clear my head after class or work... like jogging, knitting, cooking, or even just reading a book. But lately, I don't do any of that. I usually just come home, sit on my bed in my scrubs, and... I just can't make myself care about any of it anymore.
How long have you been feeling this down and unable to enjoy things?

It's been going on for about... a year and two months now. It really started right after I graduated high school, which was when I began taking college classes and started working full-time at the clinic.
During this past year, have there been periods of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?

Yeah, definitely. It's been pretty much every day. Like I was saying before, most days I wake up with that heavy, empty feeling. It just doesn't really go away. Even if I'm at work, trying to smile and speak Spanish with my patients and act like everything is fine, I'm really just... barely holding it together the whole time. It's definitely been happening for weeks on end, not just a day here or there.
Before this past year began, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'd have a bad day here and there in high school, but nothing like this. It never lasted for weeks at a time. This past year and a half is really the first time I've ever felt this way.
When you feel this down, have you heard voices or had experiences that other people would say weren’t real?

No, um, nothing like that. I've never heard voices or... or seen things that weren't there. It's really just the sadness and that heavy feeling I mentioned. My mind isn't playing tricks on me or anything.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually up, energized, or irritable for several days in a row?
No, I haven't. I've never really felt unusually energized or anything like that. It's just been the opposite, really. I'm just tired and down most of the time.
Over the past six months, have you been worrying excessively about several different things in your life?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things, like my nursing classes or paying bills, but it's not excessive. It's just... normal worry, I guess. Nothing that keeps me up at night or feels out of control. It's really just the depression that's the problem.
